newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products hold steady on U.S., Asian demand.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products hold steady on U.S., Asian demand.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products held steady Tuesday by demand from outside the region, traders said.

Naphtha prices held steady after falling sharply with crude futures last week, but traders said European demand was thin. Only Far East interest underpinned the market but just large cargoes were profitable.
Tighter supplies left fob cargo offers scarce with sellers holding out for higher prices. Cargoes were assessed notionally around $172/$174 cif Med.
Gasoline prices were little changed with traders looking for fresh arbitrage options to the U.S. as local demand stays thin.
Around 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes was sold to the U.S. in the second half of April, down from 800,000 tonnes in April 1996.
Eurograde cargoes valued around $205 with NYMEX unleaded hovering just above and offering little fresh arb opportunity.

Gas oil premiums were mainly steady, with May IPE $1 firmer at $166.75 at 1710 GMT. Interest in low sulphur diesel was minimal and availability was fair with some brokers predicting an arb to NWE where they said values were expected to firm.
Availability of 0.05 percent diesel remains fair after a cargo moved at a $2.50 premium over high fob Med basis Sicily.
Traders saw good demand from Lebanon for one percent, with around a $3 premium over fob Med basis Sicily for prompt cargo.
Fuel oil markets were balanced, with bunker demand muted and reasonable supplies of high sulphur cracked. However, activity was limited and prices remained broadly stable.
"There is no consistent interest in this market with all the holidays at the moment," said one trader, who was hurrying to conclude something before Thursday's Ascension Day break.
Black Sea straight-runs were heard to be plentiful, with at least one forced to find a home in the bunker market on Friday.
